title: Electors of Mainz and Cologne to Geleen, 22 October 1633: unpublished, read in part (84.2%)

steps.what: Known keys Camerarius 1621, Rákóczi 1632, Kurz 1638-39 tested by a frozen applicability criterion: none applies.
Key K from the letter minus held-out lines (German 4-gram model, then three corrections from the clear context).
One measurement on held-out lines P3.1-P3.5 (186 cipher letters): M5 0.656 vs 200 controls max 0.113; M_lm -2.512 vs max -4.182.
Whole letter decoded with K unchanged and read by Daniel's rule: 84.2% (binding losses on fol. 184v).

outcome.method_basis: Simple substitution of two-digit numbers inside German clear text; key by annealing on the letter minus five held-out lines, validated on them.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Daniel's rule (reading.md): 221 cipher words, 151 certain, 35 probable, 8 restored, 27 unresolved; certain + probable = 186/221.

validation.notes: Contributor's pre-registered held-out test (not docs/_validate.py): protocol hashed before transcription; key K frozen; one measurement on lines P3.1-P3.5 (186 cipher letters, never used for the key): M5 (share of letters covered by German words >= 5 letters) 0.656 vs 200 shuffled-key controls max 0.113 (median 0.000); M_lm -2.512 vs max -4.182. Threshold fixed in advance: M5 >= 0.60 and above all controls on both measures.

credits.note: transcription, key K recovered and validated on held-out lines; letter read in part (84.2%)
WAINUT found the lead (no. 2183): this ciphered letter in BSB Clm 10406 (Camerariana 56).

gaps.item: 19 words lost in the binding gutter of fol. 184v (microfilm of the bound volume)

texts.label: Electors of Mainz and Cologne to Geleen, 22 Oct 1633 (BSB Clm 10406 no. 206)
texts.summary: In the autumn of 1633 the Catholic League had almost no army left in the north. Hildesheim was besieged by the troops of Brunswick-Lüneburg, allies of the Swedes; Kniphausen and Melander’s Hessians held the County of Mark. The Archbishop-Elector of Mainz, Anselm Casimir Wambolt von Umstadt, in exile at Cologne, and the Elector of Cologne, Ferdinand of Bavaria, answered Gottfried Huyn von Geleen, the League’s major-general (Generalwachtmeister), on 22 October. The letter, signed in their own hands, is in clear, but everything about troops, money and people is in cipher: about 1,180 two-digit numbers slipped into the sentences. There is no contemporary decipherment on the document. We publish the reading as far as we could take it, gaps included: 84.2% of the cipher words. Most of the rest is lost in the binding of the volume, invisible on the digitised microfilm.

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 (German, read in part): fol. 184r reads throughout (relief of besieged Hildesheim, advice to Bönninghausen, Kniphausen joined with the Hessians, at least a thousand horse for Geleen); fol. 184v loses its line ends in the binding (3,000 reichsthalers by bill of exchange, a larger sum counted to Lerchenfeld, expenses to be repaid); fol. 185r reads throughout (reward promised by 'den sambtlichen unirten catholischen bundsstanden'; the Hamburg correspondent Menselius and a Jew held by Geleen). 221 words, 151 certain, 35 probable, 8 restored, 27 unresolved = 84.2%, so grade B and read in part. Key validated by one measurement on held-out lines (M5 0.656 vs controls max 0.113).

prior.where: DECODE (no Clm 103xx/104xx); this repository (no folder, origin/main c9e114cb); Cryptiana; Halm 1874 catalogue (listed only); Bierther, Briefe und Akten NF II/8 (1982), not online, Google Books snippet search negative for this letter and for Menselius; Wikipedia/ADB on Geleen.

human: Brice Dudout chose the target from the catalogue and set the rules (frozen key before validation, held-out checks, prior-work search the day of publication); AI agents transcribed, solved, checked and wrote up. Doubtful signs were settled by targeted visual review where stated.
